swaps.old_row: | J-A68.83 | Chose one light model over a per-tile surface layer — per pixel a normal, a height above the tile's datum and the unlit coverage — with a slab list for casters whose covered ground the view draws (a sky island under ghost or offset occlusion, the span marks over a passage, a deck over drawn water), brightness the sum over sources of inverse-square light with the smooth cutoff (1 − x⁴)² at each light's radius, a soft visibility marched from the surface toward the source at the source's height, ambient occlusion from the horizon in eight directions and a bounce spill — the blurred direct light's excess over the pixel's own, max(0, B(D) − D) — over a single-valued height field alone or ground-only projected shadows, because the owner's points 3 and 4 ask for exactly these properties — shadows as gradients and the absence of one light, cancelled where other lights reach, indirect light lifting them, a tall shadow crossing and shortened on a lower roof but never climbing a taller one, fall-off with "optimal distances" — while a slab is needed only where the ground under an overhang is drawn (a crown's ground is never seen from above, so crowns stay in the field); `ink` takes the light in value only, keeping its restraint. Restated in the repair round (VRC-04, VRC-07): the spill is bounce only, over blurring the whole direct light, because that spill lifted open level ground 5–7 % above its albedo (`ink` +5.3 %, `lit` +6.8 %) and moved item 69's paper target on the lit map, while bounce light is by nature the lift of a darker pixel by its lit surroundings, zero on uniform ground, so E_key = E_g · (a + sin 45°) holds exactly (`amendc_repair_rendering_r1_light.out` (C)); and the visibility is marched by one law — N samples at t_k = T · ((k + ½) ÷ N)², N = 32 for the global light and 24 for a point light, T set by the source, the pixel and the surface alone — which the CPU reference, the GPU pass and the light map's bake all use, over a sample count per implementation, because §13.4 can hold the GPU pass to the reference only where both sample the same points (§8.4; item 68, rulings 3 and (a)–(c)). |
swaps.new_row: | J-A68.83 | Chose one light model over a per-tile surface layer — per pixel a normal, a height above the tile's datum and the unlit coverage — with a slab list for casters whose covered ground the view draws (a sky island under ghost or offset occlusion, the span marks over a passage, a deck over drawn water), brightness the sum over sources of inverse-square light with the smooth cutoff (1 − x⁴)² at each light's radius, a soft visibility found along the ray from the surface toward the source at the source's height, ambient occlusion from the horizon in eight directions and a bounce spill — the blurred direct light's excess over the pixel's own, max(0, B(D) − D) — over a single-valued height field alone or ground-only projected shadows, because the owner's points 3 and 4 ask for exactly these properties — shadows as gradients and the absence of one light, cancelled where other lights reach, indirect light lifting them, a tall shadow crossing and shortened on a lower roof but never climbing a taller one, fall-off with "optimal distances" — while a slab is needed only where the ground under an overhang is drawn (a crown's ground is never seen from above, so crowns stay in the field); `ink` takes the light in value only, keeping its restraint. Restated in the repair round (VRC-04, VRC-07): the spill is bounce only, over blurring the whole direct light, because that spill lifted open level ground 5–7 % above its albedo (`ink` +5.3 %, `lit` +6.8 %) and moved item 69's paper target on the lit map, while bounce light is by nature the lift of a darker pixel by its lit surroundings, zero on uniform ground, so E_key = E_g · (a + sin 45°) holds exactly (`amendc_repair_rendering_r1_light.out` (C)); and one law finds the visibility for the CPU reference, the GPU pass and the light map's bake, over a law per implementation, because §13.4 can hold the GPU pass to the reference only where both evaluate the same thing.
